bandReport.notes: LAST BAND. Items 61-80, all whole on my pages; no item starts before p32 or continues past p42. Every page in the band carried items — no empty pages. PAPER ENDS AT ITEM 80 (printed p43 = index 42). Verified rather than assumed: rendered PDF indices 43-47 myself (the paper is 48 pages; config only renders evens 2-42). Printed pages 44, 45, 46 and 47 are ALL 'SPACE FOR ROUGH WORK'; p47 carries the end-of-booklet star ornament and the back-cover show-through. So the '[ P.T.O.' printed under item 80 points at rough-work pages, not at more questions. There is no Hindi mirror after p43 either. DECIMAL SEPARATOR: RAISED MIDDLE DOT (U+00B7), confirmed at 4x zoom on item 70 - the dot sits at mid-x-height, clearly off the baseline. Preserved as printed in item 70's weightages (0.2/0.3/0.5 written with U+00B7) and in all four of its options (5.1-5.4). No other item in the band prints a decimal. SHARED PASSAGES: two, both opening and closing inside my band, so no cross-band context risk. (i) 'Directions for the next 2 (two) items' on p32 - the Hugh Grant / Wimbledon passage governs items 61 and 62. (ii) 'Directions for the next 2 (two) items' on p34 - the convergence-theory passage governs items 63 and 64. Each passage composed once and assigned byte-identically to both its items (verified programmatically). Items 65-80 are standalone and carry no context. GLYPH CONVENTIONS: the booklet sets apostrophes and quotes as curly (U+2019/U+2018/U+201C/U+201D); transcribed as straight ASCII to match the shipped house convention across every prior Paper II band in this corpus, which is overwhelmingly straight. Em dashes in the item-63/64 passage are genuine U+2014 as printed. 'List-I'/'List-II' in items 72, 73 and 75 are printed with an EN DASH (U+2013), confirmed at 3x zoom against the hyphen and against the footer's TDMN-B-AST dashes; preserved as printed, which differs from the 2026-p1 bands' 'List I' spacing - that is the source, not a slip. Rupee amounts in items 78 and 80 use the printed rupee sign with a following space, matching shipped convention. LINE-BREAK HYPHENATION resolved in item 73: List-II entry 2 is set 'confiden-tially' across two lines and is transcribed 'confidentially'; entry 4's 'non-targeted' is a genuine compound hyphen and is kept. FEET/PRIME MARKS in item 68 confirmed at 3x zoom (3' x 3', 3' x 7', 3' x 11', 3' x 100') and written inside LaTeX zones. TABLES: item 70 is a genuine 4-column data grid and items 72, 73, 75 are List-I/List-II matches - all four written as GFM pipe tables with the mandatory separator row; the match-list code options follow the shipped 'A-1, B-3, C-4, D-2' form. NO DEFECTS FOUND: no duplicate option text anywhere in the band, no missing or unreadable item, no number skipped, no figure-dependent item. COLUMN CROPS: all twelve crops (6 pages x 2) were clean - no sliced line, no missing item number at the top of c2, no bleed from the neighbouring column. Reading order was c1 top-to-bottom then c2 top-to-bottom throughout; no item spans the gutter. BAND BOUNDARY: verified safe. My first page opens a fresh 'Directions for the next 2 (two) items' block, so no passage is shared across the 60/61 seam and no context of mine needs to match the sibling band byte-for-byte. FOR THE MERGE, a verified divergence worth knowing: the sibling band 2026-p2.b3.json (items 41-60) transcribes apostrophes as CURLY (U+2019/U+2018) where this band uses straight ASCII. Harmless here because no passage crosses the seam, but the two bands are not glyph-consistent with each other, and if any later band shares a passage across a seam that difference is exactly what breaks set grouping. Flagged, not touched - it is not my file. (An earlier draft of this note claimed that file carried mojibake em dashes; I re-checked and it does not - that reading was of an in-flight state which has since been corrected, and the claim is withdrawn.)

questions.context: Was it the sun-dappled ambience, the strawberries and cream, the frustration of Flavio Cobolli's unforced errors against Serbian Novak Djokovic on Centre Court or simply the crushing weight of being a 64-year-old man in the third act of a very public life? Whatever the reason, Hugh Grant, the actor, deserves empathy. There he was, in the Royal Box at Wimbledon, flanked by Britain's well-dressed and well-rested spectators, watching the men's singles quarterfinals, when the actor did something quietly radical : head at a tilt, eyes closed, utterly unbothered, he took a nap. So praise be to Grant for serving up an unexpected ace. In that small, delicious moment, he didn't merely catch forty winks, he made an elegant case for surrender. Not to laziness, but to limits. To the body's quiet wisdom over society's relentless performance metrics. Wimbledon had its tennis. The perpetually sleep-deprived discovered a leading man, not of action, but of rest.

questions.context: The process by which countries close their labour-productivity gap with the technology leader is based on convergence theory. The convergence model divides economic eras into three phases : the breakaway, the catch-up, and the fine-tuning phase. It also divides economic entities into two categories : the technology leaders and the technology followers. The process begins with the development of a new technology, such as scavenging three million years ago (MYA), hunting—one MYA, farming—12 thousand years ago, and industrial technology—a little more than 200 years ago. During the breakaway phase, the per capita income of the technology leaders (e.g., Western Europe and North America in the industrial era) rises, but is unchanged for the technology followers. In the catch-up phase, the followers adopt the new technology and close their per capita income gap with the technology leaders. In the fine-tuning phase, where participants try to extract the remaining benefits from an increasingly exhausted technology, leaders and followers have similar per capita incomes.
questions.stem:
Which of the following conclusions are correct?
1. In the breakaway phase, economic progress is slow for the technology followers.
2. In the catch-up phase, leaders stagnate and followers, therefore, close the gap between them and the leaders.
3. In the fine-tuning phase, technology is exhausted, as it were, and both leaders and followers attempt to extract leftover benefits, leading to more or less similar per capita income levels.
4. Industrial technology followed scavenging, which preceded hunting, which itself was followed by farming.
Select the answer using the code given below.
